components.css: :host{--band:#0e1116;--band-raised:#171b22;--line:#2a313c;--ink:#fff;--ink-2:rgba(255,255,255,.78);--ink-3:#8f98a3;--sub:#f7d44c;--track-ja:#ef6a4c;--track-en:#6cb4ff;--track-vi:#f7d44c;--track-other:#a3acb7;--font:'Be Vietnam Pro','Segoe UI',system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-track{display:inline-block;min-width:26px;text-align:center;font:600 11px/1 var(--font);letter-spacing:.06em;padding:4px 6px;border-radius:3px;color:#111418;background:var(--track-other)}.ds-track[data-lang=ja]{background:var(--track-ja)}.ds-track[data-lang=en]{background:var(--track-en)}.ds-track[data-lang=vi]{background:var(--track-vi)}.ds-icon-btn{width:28px;height:28px;display:grid;place-items:center;border:0;border-radius:5px;background:transparent;color:var(--ink-3);cursor:pointer;padding:0}.ds-icon-btn:hover{color:var(--ink);background:rgba(255,255,255,.07)}.ds-icon-btn:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--sub);outline-offset:2px}.ds-icon-btn[aria-pressed=true]{color:var(--sub)}.ds-icon-btn svg{width:16px;height:16px;stroke:currentColor;fill:none;stroke-width:1.7;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-linejoin:round}.ds-pop{width:420px;font:14px/1.5 var(--font);color:var(--ink);background:var(--band);border-radius:6px;padding:10px 12px 14px 14px;box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.38),0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.3)}.ds-bar{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px}.ds-arrow{color:var(--ink-3);font-size:12px}.ds-engine{margin-left:6px;font-size:11px;color:var(--ink-3)}.ds-actions{margin-left:auto;display:flex;gap:2px}.ds-src{margin:10px 0 0;color:var(--ink-2);font-family:'Yu Gothic UI','Meiryo UI',Meiryo,sans-serif}.ds-tl{margin:4px 0 0;font-size:18px;font-weight:600;line-height:1.42;color:var(--sub);text-shadow:0 1px 0 #000,0 0 2px #000}

narrative.overview:
A translation is a subtitle laid under what the user is reading. Every surface is an opaque near-black band floating over someone else's app: the source line sits small in dimmed white, the translation reads in subtitle yellow with a hairline black outline, and languages are named by coloured track chips, the way a fansub labels its tracks. The world refuses the category default of a white card with a language dropdown and a grey translated paragraph.

Density is compact and glanceable; the popup is read mid-task and dismissed with Esc. There is one look, dark, by design: the band is a subtitle band, not a theme, so there is no light variant. Latin and Vietnamese set in Be Vietnam Pro (bundled, OFL); Japanese falls to the Windows faces Yu Gothic UI and Meiryo through `:lang(ja)`.
keyCharacteristics: Opaque near-black band, 6px corners, soft ambient shadow.
Translation in subtitle yellow with a 1px black outline shadow; source in 78% white.
Coloured language track chips are the signature: JA vermilion, EN blue, VI yellow.
Result lines reveal cue by cue (fade and 3px rise, 80ms stagger).
Thin-stroke 16px line icons in a quiet muted grey until hovered.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Subtitle yellow is the only accent. It marks the translation and the one action that matters; nothing decorative is yellow.

rules.name: The Tracks Name Languages Rule
rules.body: Vermilion, blue and grey appear only as language track chips. They never colour text, borders or buttons.

rules.name: The Readable Subtitle Rule
rules.body: The translation is always the largest weighted text in a sentence result (18px/600) and always carries the outline shadow (`0 1px 0 #000, 0 0 2px #000`); the source above it stays at 14px in dim ink.

rules.name: The Floating Band Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to the outer band only, scaled to its size; controls inside it stay flat.

dos: Do set every surface on the opaque subtitle band with 6px corners.
Do put the translation in subtitle yellow at 18px/600 with the black outline shadow.
Do name languages only with track chips (JA vermilion, EN blue, VI yellow, other grey).
Do mark Japanese runs with `lang="ja"` so they fall to Yu Gothic UI / Meiryo.
Do keep icons as 16px inline SVG line icons at 1.7 stroke in `currentColor`.
donts: Don't add a light theme or a translucent/acrylic band; the band is opaque and dark by design.
Don't fall back to a white card with a language dropdown and a grey translated paragraph.
Don't use track colours outside chips, or yellow for decoration.
Don't shadow controls inside a band.
